To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the functional expression of diheteromeres in mammalian cells is NR1 splice-variant dependent and that NR1-1/NR3A and NR1-4/NR3A diheteromere receptors have different pharmacological properties.

NR1 splice variants influence the assembly and function of diheterommeric NR1/NR1 receptors in HEK293 cells and that the NR1-2 splice variant, which has a longer C-terminal tail than the NR1- 1 splice variant, allows for robust glycine-activation in the presence of NR3A or B. This

NR1 splice variants influence the functional expression of glycine-activated NR1/NR2 receptors and that glycine-activated diheteromeres can be generated in mammalian cells by coexpression of NR1 splice variants that do not form functional receptors when expressed with NR1-1A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that control the assembly of functional NMDA receptors.
the molecular mechanisms of synaptic plasticity and the pathogenesis of neurological disease.
the molecular mechanisms underlying NMDA receptor function and dysfunction, with a particular focus on the NR1 and NR2 subunits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of NR3A and/or NR3B in combination with the NR1 splice variants NR1-2, NR1-4, and NR1-3 is sufficient for the functional expression of glycine-activated NR1/NR1/NR3A/B receptors in mammalian cell lines.
glycine-activated NR1/NR1 receptors are formed in mammalian cells, but only when NR1 splice variants other than NR1-1 are expressed.
the NR3 subunit is a unique NMDAR subunit that can form heteromeric NMDARs with NR1 subunits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glycine activates diheteromeres of NR1 and NR2 or NR1 and NR1/NR2 in the presence of NR3, and that glycine activates triheteromeres containing NR1, NR2, and NR3.
glycine-activated diheteromeres can be expressed in mammalian cells, but they require a specific NR1 splice variant.
NR1-1 is not the best splice variant for expression in mammalian cells of glycine-activated NR1/NR2 and NR1/NR4 receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NR3 receptors are not functional when coexpressed with the most common NR1 isoform, NR1-1, but are functional when coexpressing with other NR1 isoforms, including NR1-4.

NR1 splice variants are critical for the formation of functional glycine-activated NR1/NR2/NR3 receptors, but NR1 splice variants alone do not generate functional NR1/NR 3A or NR1/NR1/NR3B receptors in HEK293 cells.

glycine-activated diheterommeric receptors formed by N-methyl-d- aspartate receptor 1 (NR1) and NR3 subunit combinations are expressed in mammalian cells, but only in the presence of certain NR1 splice variants.
